issues.description: The DD dataclass weight attribute is annotated inconsistently between the template and the solution. In the template dd.py the attribute is annotated as `float` while in the solution dd.py it is annotated as `np.complex128` and the code creates ZERO_TERM and ONE_TERM with complex weights (np.complex128). This mismatch between the annotated type and how weights are actually used (complex numbers) may confuse students and cause static type-checking issues or misunderstandings about expected value types.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the type annotation of the DD.weight attribute in the template dd.py to match the solution and actual usage (use `np.complex128`) so that the declared type aligns with ZERO_TERM/ONE_TERM and the rest of the code. For example: `weight: np.complex128`. Also ensure any accompanying docstrings or comments mention that weights are complex-valued.
